the disputed property appertaining to S.A. khatian 551 comprising an area of 2.59 acres belonged to one Khirod Chandra Kapali along with Gyan Ranjan Ghose. The land of S.A. khatian No.400 comprising an 'area 3.47 acres belonged to Gyan Ranjao in eight annas share and Nakul Chandra Kapali in two annas along with the defendant No.11 Abul Hossain Howlader wakf Estate in which one Chan Mia Howlader was Mutawally of the property. Chand Miah Howlader subsequently transferred 2.69 acres of land in plot Nos.331 and 333 of S.A khatian No.400 in favour of the defendant-petitioner Barguna Govt. University College and delivered possession therein. After the death of Notobar Kapali and his five sons the plaintiff Nos.1r3 and one Monohor and others became, hears and it was decided within the parties in dispute i.e. the plaintiffs and the defendant No.1 that 43 decimals of land would be transferred by virtue of a deed of exchange. Pursuant to that 43 decimals of land in plot No.331 and 333 of S.A. khatian No.400 is being possessed by1ehe plaintiffs, but due to a conflict upon the boundary of the land; to get the land by partition through Court the plaintiffs filed by the original suit being No.1 14 of 2004 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant No.1 is such that the defendant Barguna Govt. College was established in the year 1969 and at the time of its inception Hazi Chand Miah Howlader by a registered sub-kabala deed dated 14.06.1969 transferred 1.20 acres of land in favour of the defendant No.1 and Gyan Ranjan Ghose by a deed of gift transferred 1.49 acres of land in S.A. khatian No.400 and 46 decimals of land in S.A. khatian No.802 in favour of the defendant. Thereafter the defendant-petitioner in the entire land comprising an area of 3.15 acres in plot Nos.323, 333 and 327 had been possessing after erecting a building for Barguna College. The further case of the defendant is such that the land of plot Nos.331 and 333 in S.A. khatian No.400 measuring 60 decimals are being possess by the defendant No. 1 since 1969 openly and aversely within the knowledge of all and thus acquired title by way of adverse possession. The defendant-petitioner denied the exchange with the plaintiff-opposite-parties as alleged and it is their case that the land measuring 60 decimals in the suit plot Nos.331 and 333 are not vacant, only 40 decimal of land out of those two plots remain vacant which is tinder the possession of the defendant-petitioner. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the, plaintiff-opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the trial Court during disposal of the original suit and the appellate Court at the time of deciding the fate of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The evidence lead from the sides of the respective parties were thoroughly evaluated by both the courts below and it was the concurrent observation and decision of the learned trial Court as well as the appellate Court that the plaintiff-opposite parties have exclusive possession and title over the suit property and by virtue of the talk of exchange the plaintiffs do possess the suit land measuring 43 decimals in plot Nos.331 and 331 of S.A. khatian No.400 and by sufficient competent cogent evidence the plaintiffs proved their case as regard talk of exchange. They have examined the admitted member of the governing body of the defendant college the witness No.5 Abdul Mannan who has corroborated the case of the plaintiffs in toto and beside this the remaining witnesses of the plaintiffs proved the positive assertion of the plaintiff's case. The witness No.1 who is a man of 80 years, deposed in the support of the case and he is corroborated by the witness No.2 Nur Mohammad, witness No.3 Subol Chandra Roy and witness No.4 Nitai Chandra Samaddar. On the contrary the only witness adduced from the side of the defendant the witness No.1 Md. Younus Miah not at all was able to prove the case of the defendant rather falsified the claim of the defendant who is not competent to depose on behalf of the defendant college. The learned Advocate for the opposite-parties further submits that it is an extraneous case of the defendant-petitioner that the entire land lies within the college compound because exhibit No.3 the admitted deed of exchange between the college and Mahila Sangstha of Barguna go to show that within the plaintiff's claimed plot Nos.331 and 333 in S.A. khatian No.400 the defendant-petitioner have got other land out of their boundary wall in which the Mahila Sangstha is possessing. The learned counsel for the opposite-parties lastly submits that the title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land as described by them in the contents of their plaint has been well proved by adequate competent evidence and there was no legal embargo from the side of the Court to award decree as prayed for. The defendant-petitioner in their written statement in para 18 clearly admits that 40 decimals of land in the suit plots being Nos.331 and 333 is vacant. By way of 'away which was held orally between the parties the defendant-petitioner went into possession of the plaintiff's land and by virtue of the very `away (exchange) the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land measuring 43 decimals, but since the exchange was not done in writing the defendant-petitioner tried to disturb the possession of the plaintiffs and as a result of which the plaintiffs instituted the suit for partition. 

 9. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the case record, exhibited documents, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. On perusal of the case record it transpires that admittedly the plaintiffs after the demise of recorded tenant Notobar Kapali in S.A. khatian No.551 inherited his share while the Motawali Chand Miah Howlader of Abul Hossein Howlader Waqf State transferred 1.20 acres of land from plot No.331 and 1.49 acres of land from plot No.333 in S.A. khatian No.400 by a registered kabala deed in favour of the defendant-petitioner and the said transfer deeds has been marked exhibits during trial. The subject matter in dispute between the parties is as to whether there was in fact a talk of 'awaj' (exchange) transfer in respect of the suit land measuring 43 decimals, The positive case of the plaintiffs is such that by .virtue of that awaj their land which was transferred in favour of the contesting-defendant stands within the college premises in where the defendant-petitioner do possess and side by side pursuant to the aforesaid awaj the suit land measuring 43 decimals is under the possession of the plaintiffs from the very beginning. The fact remains that the defendant-petitioner's specific contention is such that the land of the plaintiff-opposite-parties is under their forcible possession for more that twelve years and in that land they have got adverse possession and in fact there is no existence of awaj transfer between them. 

 10. In support of the plaintiffs case they have adduced as many as 5 witnesses. The witness No.1 is the plaintiff No.2 of the original suit. In his deposition he states supporting their oral awaj on 2e Poush, 1376 B.S. corresponding to 12m January, 1970. Plaintiff No.2 claims that they amicably handed over the possession of their 43 decimals of land to college from the northern side of the college compound and in exchange college amicably handed over possession of their land in which they are possessing by cultivation. In his deposition the plaintiff No.2 specifically states to the effect that the suit land is the ejmali land of the co-sharers and there was no partition. The witness No.2 Nur Mohammad states at a stage that he knows the parties and the suit land and by way of `awaj' transfer the defendant handed over possession of 43 decimals of land in plot Nos.331 and 333 of S.A. khatian No.400 in favour of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs handed over the same quantum of land in favour of the defendant from plot Nos.269 and 320 of khatian No.551 and this witness was present at the time of 'away which was held on 12m January, 1970 A.D. The witness No.3 for the plaintiffs states in support of the possession of the plaintiffs by way of oral `awaj'. The witness No.4 for the plaintiffs is a contiguous land owner of the suit land. He also states in support of the plaintiff's possession of the suit land measuring 43 decimals by virtue of oral 'awn' between the parties. The last witness for the plaintiffs Md. Abdul Mannan states in his deposition that he knows the parties and he joined as a member of Barguna College Governing body from the very inception of Barguna College and at that time in the year 1969 he was Union Parishad Member. In his deposition this witness further states that at the time of creation of the college there has been some oral `awaj'. 

 11. Vis-a-vis; the witness No. 1 for the defendant-petitioner Md. Younus Miah who is a college staff states in his deposition that the defendant Barguna Govt. College after its creation in the year 1969 possess the land measuring 43 decimals in plot No.320 and 269 in S.A. khatian No.551. Them was no talk of awaj between them and the plaintiffs and they possess the suit land forcibly. This witness specifically states at a stage that since 01.07.1969 they possess the suit land forcibly and he admits that he does not know as to why 43 decimals of land was acquired forcibly and he was not present at that time. He admits in his deposition that in their college there lies no resolution to that effect. At a stage this witness expressed his inability to state the quantum of land of plot No.320 and 269 in which the college authority allegedly possess. 

 14. From the evidence on record it is evident to note that save an except same minor discrepancies, the deposition of the plaintiff No.2. who was the old man of 81 years the other witnesses for the plaintiffs has been successfully proved the case of the plaintiffs. The specific contention as it appears that the defendant by virtue of oral awaj transferred the suit land measuring 43 decimals in S.A. khatian No.400 and the plaintiffs handed over the same quantum of land from S.A. khatian No.551 which lies in plot Nos.269 and 320 has been reflected in the admission of the defendant's sole witness D.W.I Md. Younus Miah who in his examination-in-chief specifically admits the positive case of the plaintiffs by stating “আমি অত্র মামলায় অনুমতি নিয়ে জবানবন্দি করছি। ১নং বিবাদী বরগুনা সরকারী কলেজ ১��৬৯ সালে প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়। প্রতিষ্ঠালগ্ন হতে হাজী চান মিয়া ১৪/০৬/৬৯ তাং এস. এ. ৪০০নং খতিয়ান হতে ১ একর ২০ শতাংশ জমি কলেজ বরাবরে হস্তান্তর করে। জ্ঞানারঞ্জন ঘোষ ৩১/০৭/৭২ তাং এস. এ. ৪০০/৮০২ নং খতিয়ানন হতে ১ একর ৯৫ শতাংশ জমি জলেজে দান করে। আমরা মোট ২ একর ১৫ শতাংশ জমিতে কলেজ নির্মিত করি। আমরা তাতে ভোগ দখল করি। এতে এস.এ. ৫৫১ নং খতিয়ানে ৩২০/২৬৯ নং দাগে ৪৩ শতাংশ জমি ঐ কলেজের ভোগ দখল আছে। আমরা জবর দখল করি।” The very admission of the defendant's witness makes it is clear that in fact there was a talk of oral awaj between the parties and it was affected duly. Nowhere in the college record admittedly there exist any such resolution that the suit land have been possessed forcibly and the witness also admits that there cannot be any principle, rule or system of such acquisition of land forcibly. Both the Courts below in this context were quite justified that the educational institution must have to maintain some sanctity and ethics and none should support that an institution can acquire or retain possession of any land forcibly. This sort of illegal immoral act is not at all expected from an educational institution. Be that as it may; the Court of law must not protect such misdeed. Both the Courts below concurrently found in their judgment and decisions that the plaintiff-opposite-parties successfully discharged the onus of proving their respective case and the appellate Court being the final Court of facts decided that there was in fact an oral awaj between the parties by virtue of which the disputed land was handed over to the plaintiffs and they do possess the same.
